name: alert
description: UIDS alert component contract, preserving the verified 4.x rendering and documenting the proposed Figma representation.

figma.note: BUILT (Phase 3). 16 variants: Color (Info, Success, Warning, Danger) x Icon (No Icon, With Icon) x Dismissible (Without, With Close Button).
axisRationale: The Button/Headline Style-axis collapse was evaluated for Icon+Dismissible and REJECTED: merging two independent 2-value booleans into one enumerated axis still produces 2x2=4 values either way, so there is no variant-count reduction — and two separate boolean axes give a clearer per-property toggle in Figma's variant picker than one composite 4-value 'Display' axis.

The collapse that IS applied is the Button borderless/full pattern: centered and verticallyCentered are excluded from the axis set and stay code-only. Without that exclusion the naive matrix would be 4 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 = 64.
Combinations beyond the three chosen axes (e.g. centered + dismissible together) are code-only via props, per each option's figma.notes.
figma.precedent: Button (borderless/full excluded from the axis set).

options.name: type
options.description: Colorway and icon glyph. Drives the alert--{type} background/icon-color modifier class AND, via a separate computed property, which Font Awesome glyph renders (success->check, warning->exclamation-triangle, danger->exclamation, default/fallback->info) — two independent code paths keyed off one prop value.

code.notes: Alert.vue's validator strictly allows only these 4 strings (indexOf check, Alert.vue:14-16) — unlike Button's color prop, there is no dead/undefined accepted value to flag here; this enum is clean.

options.name: iconVisible
options.description: Renders the leading icon block. Gates a structural v-if (Alert.vue:93-95) — the fa-stack/fa-circle markup only exists in the DOM when true — in addition to adding the alert--icon class (display:flex, turning the alert into a two-column row).

code.notes: Vue prop name (iconVisible) does not mechanically derive the CSS class name (alert--icon, not alert--icon-visible) — handled by its own dedicated branch in the classes computed, not the generic className() loop.

options.name: dismissible
options.description: Renders a close button. Gates a structural v-if (Alert.vue:97-99) — the whole <button data-dismiss="alert"> only exists when true — in addition to adding the alert--dismissible class (position:relative, so the button can be absolutely positioned).

code.notes: The actual removal-on-click behavior is not implemented anywhere in this repo — see behavior and identity.downstreamPaths.

options.name: centered
options.description: Horizontally centers content via display:flex + justify-content:center.

code.notes: Applied via the generic ['centered','dismissible'].forEach loop (Alert.vue:80-84) through the className() utility, which only replaces underscores with hyphens — a no-op for this single-word prop name.

figma.notes: Deliberately NOT a variant axis — same treatment as Button's borderless/full. centered and verticallyCentered are independent, freely-combinable flex modifiers whose difference is a repositioning, not a distinct look, and doubling the matrix to 64 variants for two rarely-combined booleans has no navigational value. Reinforced by usage evidence, not just aesthetics: uids_base's status-messages.html.twig (the only known real-world consumer) never sets centered at all — it is exclusively a direct-Vue/Storybook-only option today. Code-only for any combination beyond the three chosen axes.

options.name: verticallyCentered
options.description: Vertically centers content via display:flex + align-items:center.

figma.notes: Deliberately NOT a variant axis — see centered's figma.notes. Unlike centered, this one IS always forced on by the one known downstream consumer (status-messages.html.twig hardcodes alert--vertically-centered unconditionally), so it is live in production, just still not axis-worthy on its own visual merits.

slots.name: default
slots.description: The alert's body content (falls back to the literal text "Body" if none provided, Alert.vue:96). Consumers commonly place heading tags (h2-h6) here, which pick up Alert's own private --h2-font-size-driven scale rather than the site's global heading tokens.
slots.behavior: The `class="alert__content"` written directly on the <slot> element (Alert.vue:96) is DEAD. Verified by compiling the actual template with @vue/compiler-sfc: it emits `_renderSlot(_ctx.$slots, "default", { class: "alert__content" }, ...)` — i.e. Vue treats a non-name attribute on <slot> as a SCOPED-SLOT PROP, not a rendered DOM attribute. No consumer in either repo destructures it (`v-slot="{ class }"`), and no CSS anywhere targets `.alert__content` — fully inert. Do not model it as a real hook in Figma or elsewhere. See claims/knownIssues.

figma.notes: Modelled as a text/content region bound to the instance — the same role Button/Headline give their default slot.

behavior: type drives both the color modifier class and (via Alert.vue's separate `icon` computed, lines 48-63) which Font Awesome glyph renders — the glyph choice is coupled to type, not independently configurable.

iconVisible and dismissible each gate a structural v-if block (the icon markup / the close button), not merely a CSS class. centered and verticallyCentered only ever add a class — no structural change.

dismissible's actual removal-on-click behavior is implemented ENTIRELY downstream in uiowa/uiowa's uids_base theme: assets/js/uids.status-messages.js registers Drupal.behaviors.uidsStatusMessages, a delegated body click-listener matching `button[data-dismiss='alert']`, which walks up to `.closest('.alert--dismissible')`, fades its opacity over 0.3s, then removes the node after a 300ms timeout. UIDS itself ships ZERO JS for this — a Storybook dismiss button renders but does nothing on click unless a consumer wires the same handler. Record via identity.downstreamPaths so nobody concludes the feature is non-functional because src/assets/js/ has no matching class.

Border: `.alert` includes the shared border mixin (@include utilities.border, _utilities.scss:193-199), which the border foundation contract (contracts/border.json, already migrated in Phase 2) fully resolves to color/border/default (default context) and color/border/on-dark (inside `[class*="bg--black"]` ancestors). contracts/border.json's own identity.relatedPaths already names alert.scss as a consumer. No new border tokens are minted by this contract — Alert's Figma set should bind the EXISTING semantic variables, not re-derive them.

Downstream (uids_base status-messages.html.twig -> alert.html.twig) hardcodes alert_dismissible:true and the classes alert--icon + alert--vertically-centered unconditionally for every Drupal status message — there is no Drupal-side equivalent of iconVisible=false, verticallyCentered=false, or centered=true/false at all (centered is never set downstream). Every production Drupal alert is therefore icon-visible + vertically-centered + dismissible by construction; only the Color axis and (indirectly) content actually vary in practice.

Downstream's role handling is richer than Alert.vue's: status-messages.html.twig:51 computes `alert_role` dynamically — `(type == 'error' or type == 'warning') ? 'alert' : 'status'` — giving error/warning messages an assertive `role="alert"` live region and status/info messages a polite `role="status"` live region, then alert.html.twig:24 renders `aria-label="{{ alert_type }} message"` on the container. None of this exists in Alert.vue, whose root <div> carries no role or aria-label at all. See knownIssues/a11y.

Downstream's alert_type vocabulary (Drupal message types: status/warning/error, mapped to alert--success/--warning/--dan​ger; a fourth 'info' branch exists in alert.html.twig but requires a caller to explicitly pass a non-standard 'info' message type since Drupal core's Messenger only emits status/warning/error) differs from Vue's `type` vocabulary (info/success/warning/danger) — a naming-layer translation, not a functional gap; out of this contract's scope to verify further since it lives entirely in the downstream repo's custom-module surface.
knownIssues: Alert.vue's outer <div> (line 92) carries no `role` and no `aria-label`; its dismiss <button> (line 97) carries no `aria-label` or `type` attribute either. Downstream's uids_base chain independently computes and adds all of these (see behavior) — the canonical Storybook/Vue rendering is measurably, and in more ways than a single missing label, less accessible than what ships to production. See openQuestions (whether this migration also patches Alert.vue).

$danger and $orange are the identical hex #BD472A (_variables.scss:12,19); the warning state's icon (alert.scss:81, $orange) and the danger state's icon (alert.scss:65, $danger) render in the bit-identical color. Already resolved at the primitive tier — tokens/primitives/colors.json's color.status.danger carries the comment '4.x: $danger / $orange' — reused here, not re-minted. See claims.

Lightness scaling is inconsistent across the four states: danger-light/warning-light use color.scale($x, $lightness: 85%) (_variables.scss:18,20) while success-light/info-light use 95% (_variables.scss:14,16) — success (#EBFFFA) and info (#EDF8FF) render visibly lighter than danger (#F7E2DD) and warning (#FFF8D9). Tokenized as-shipped (four independent primitives); flagged as a 5.x normalization candidate, not fixed here.

The H2-H6 internal scale is authored as one base custom property plus calc() ratio multipliers, which Figma text styles cannot bind. Resolved here as 5 independent concrete tier-3 tokens (h2 reuses the existing typography.font-size.400 primitive; h3-h6 are raw literals). See openQuestions for the base+ratio alternative the input survey flagged.

$content-font-size (alert.scss:11,55) is the pre-existing typography.body.font-size semantic composite's value (already var(--uiowa-font-size-body)-driven, _variables.scss:70) — NOT alert-exclusive vocabulary. Not claimed as a new tier-3 token; no SCSS swap is even needed for it (already fully token-driven pre-migration). See claims.
`class="alert__content"` on the default <slot> (Alert.vue:96) compiles to an unused scoped-slot prop, never read by any consumer and matching no CSS — dead. See claims.
`const name = 'uids-alert'` (Alert.vue:6) is declared and never read — the same dead-code pattern already documented for Button ('uids-button') and Headline ('uids-headine', itself typo'd).

alert.scss:96's section-boundary comment reads `// === End: Alert Icon === //` but actually closes the 'Alert Colors' section opened at alert.scss:60 — the genuine Alert Icon section already has its own correct closing comment at alert.scss:58. Copy-paste mislabel, comment-only, zero rendering effect.

Font Awesome rendering mode differs between this repo's Storybook and actual production, independent of anything alert.scss controls: .storybook/preview-head.html:4 loads FA via a plain webfont CSS CDN link (no JS replacement), while uiowa/uiowa's exported Drupal config (config/default/fontawesome.settings.yml: method: svg, use_cdn: true, external_svg_location pointing at FA's real all.js SVG kit) means production DOES run FA's SVG auto-replacement script, which rewrites <i>/<span class="fas ..."> elements into <svg class="svg-inline--fa ..."> at runtime. This is why uids_base's OWN theme-level scss/components/alert.scss (a file distinct from its byte-identical vendored mirror of this repo's alert.scss) carries its own extra rules against the identical `.svg-inline--fa.fa-stack-2x`/`.fa-stack-1x` selectors under an explicit '// SVG in JS style adjustments for alert icon.' comment — real, intentional, production-only styling that has no observable effect in this repo's Storybook. See claims.

Alert.vue's dismiss-button icon uses an `<i>` tag (line 98), while every other icon element in the same file (lines 94, and the downstream Twig template's equivalent markup) uses `<span>`. Given the production FA SVG-replacement script likely operates on class patterns rather than tag names, the practical rendering consequence of this inconsistency could not be confirmed via static analysis — flagged as an open question rather than a firm defect.

alert.scss:11 still hardcodes `font-size: variables.$content-font-size` -- the alert body font-size was never tokenized (there is no alert/font-size token, unlike every other alert value). The Figma component binds its body text to the font/size/150 primitive instead. Ruled 2026-08-16: record rather than fix, so the verified swap commit stays untouched. Candidate for a follow-up token addition.

Alert.vue gates `dismissible` two different ways: the CLASS through the shared ['centered','dismissible'] forEach, which tests `props[prop] === true` (Alert.vue:80-84), and the BUTTON through `v-if="props.dismissible"` (Alert.vue:97), which is bare truthiness. Because the prop is `type: Boolean` with no default, Vue coerces an absent attribute to false and the two agree today, so this is latent rather than live. It is the SAME shape as the icon defect fixed 2026-08-20 in claude-design/Alert.dc.html, which did become visible precisely because that prop's effective default was true: `undefined` is falsy but `undefined !== false` is true, so the class dropped while the element still rendered. Recorded, not fixed, per tokenize-as-shipped; the fix belongs in Alert.vue (one predicate, or route dismissible through the same forEach as centered), not in the Claude Design mirror, which is currently faithful. Surfaced by check-claude-design.mjs check 6.

geometryNotTokenized.sibling-spacing-reset: .alert * { margin-bottom: 0; & + *:not(span):not(div):not(svg) { margin-top: .2rem; line-height: 1.6; } } (alert.scss:30-37) — generic content-flow/rhythm reset for arbitrary slotted markup, not a themeable design value. Note: by specificity, (.alert * + *:not(span):not(div):not(svg) = (0,1,3)) beats (.alert = (0,1,0)), so only the FIRST child in any alert actually renders at the tokenized alert/line-height (1.3); every subsequent non-span/div/svg sibling renders at 1.6 instead (which coincidentally equals the existing typography.line-height.160 primitive, itself not claimed here since this whole rule stays untokenized).
geometryNotTokenized.warning-icon-nudge: .fa-exclamation-triangle { margin-top: -2px; } (alert.scss:84-86) — hard pixel nudge tied to that specific Font Awesome glyph's metrics, same treatment class as Button's Antonio font-weight caveat; not a design value.
geometryNotTokenized.icon-stack-mechanics: .alert__icon .fa-stack { width: 2em } (alert.scss:45-47) deliberately narrows Font Awesome's own default .fa-stack width (2.5em, all.css:307-313) via a higher-specificity override (0-2-0 beats 0-1-0) — a real, live design choice, but expressed in em (relative to inherited font-size context) rather than an isolable absolute dimension, so left as documented geometry rather than a tier-3 token. .svg-inline--fa.fa-stack-2x/-1x { width: 100% } (alert.scss:49-52) is unreachable in this repo's own Storybook and, even where reachable downstream, duplicates FA's own already-active .fa-stack-1x/-2x{width:100%} base rule (all.css:315-321) — see claims and knownIssues.
geometryNotTokenized.dismiss-button-positioning: .alert--dismissible button { position: absolute; right: 0; top: 0; background: transparent; border: none; } (alert.scss:118-122) — placement/reset mechanics, not tokenized; only the button's size (alert/dismiss/size) and icon size (alert/dismiss/icon-font-size) are.
geometryNotTokenized.border: The 1px border and its bg--black color flip come entirely from the shared border foundation (@include utilities.border, contracts/border.json — already migrated, already names alert.scss as a consumer). Alert consumes, does not re-mint, color/border/default and color/border/on-dark.
